title: Global and Local Inversions
summary: Given an integer array representing a permutation of [0, n-1], determine if the count of global inversions (pairs (i, j) where i nums[j]) equals the count of local inversions (pairs (i, i+1) where nums[i] > nums[i+1]).
statement: Given an integer array representing a permutation of [0, n-1], determine if the count of global inversions (pairs (i, j) where i nums[j]) equals the count of local inversions (pairs (i, i+1) where nums[i] > nums[i+1]).
constraints: nums is a permutation of 0 through n-1.
Return whether every global inversion is also adjacent.
hints: A nonlocal inversion exists exactly when an element exceeds some value at least two positions right.
Sweep backward while tracking the minimum beyond the adjacent position.
For i from n-3 down, update minimum from i+2 and reject nums[i]>minimum.
The maintained suffix minimum witnesses every possible nonlocal inversion in linear time.
editorial: The maintained suffix minimum witnesses every possible nonlocal inversion in linear time.

tests.explanation: The only inversion is the adjacent pair 1,0.
The pair 1,0 is a nonlocal inversion.
